rationale.complete: Rounds 1 and 2 done. Round 2 (R3, R4, R1): dated pre-registration and pre-data amendment; synthetic validation of every estimator on real call grids (R4 failed and is labelled descriptive); the R3 ladder of 11 rungs on identical pairs; the R1 chat clock with a call-skeleton null (post hoc); estimates rows; period READMEs. Missing: reserved-data run (R2), the pair-sampling term, a valid multi-hop design.
rationale.faithfulness: The read-out gain is identified (synthetic bias <= 5%). It passes an unfitted cross-check against an independent fluctuation statistic: g_lag 0.127 vs the Fano-implied 0.149 [0.123, 0.175] (H111 data). The H50 disagreement is located: pair-RD design in regime III, call-class composition in regime I. H50's estimator fails synthetic recovery. The HH's own signature still fails, and the multi-hop gain is not resolved. Scorecard r2 A1 B1 C1 D2 E1 F2 G1 H2 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A calibrated, field-free loop-gain gauge computable from call logs, with an independent fluctuation check. The operator message: the equal-time dial and pair-RD jumps overstate coupling, naming carries it, regime-I talk follows the schedule, and the village is far from talk runaway. A monitor, not a lever.

one_line: Read-out talk coupling is subcritical (g_lag 0.13 in regime III, matching the Fano-implied 0.149 [0.123, 0.175]; ~0 in regime I on either clock); H50's 2x larger value is an estimator artifact.
